quotes.quote: Typhoon Liss made landfall near Sonholt on Monday, forcing the port to suspend all container operations.
The Sonholt Port Authority said on Monday evening that it estimated damage to port facilities at 42 million dollars.
The authority said three ship-to-shore cranes were knocked off their rails by the storm.
No port workers were injured, the authority said.
Engineers will inspect the quays before the port reopens.
Typhoon Liss made landfall near Sonholt on Monday, forcing the port to suspend all container operations.
The Sonholt Port Authority said on Monday evening that it estimated damage to port facilities at 42 million dollars.
The authority said three ship-to-shore cranes were knocked off their rails by the storm.
Shipping lines have begun diverting vessels to Vantage and other nearby ports while the terminal is closed.

The Sonholt Port Authority said on Tuesday that it had raised its estimate of damage to port facilities to 95 million dollars, from the 42 million dollars it announced on Monday evening, after inspectors found cracks in two quays.
The authority said a fourth ship-to-shore crane was found damaged during Tuesday's inspection.
No port workers were injured, the authority added.
